import CoolProp.CoolProp as CP

# Check available fluids and fluid name for Freon-12 (R12)
fluid = 'R12'
print('Fluid name:', fluid)
# Let's inspect density at various T and P
# Marianas trench:
# Depth = ~10994 m to 11034 m
# Sea water density: average ~1025 to 1050 kg/m^3, pressure at depth ~ 108.6 to 110 MPa (1086 to 1100 bar, ~1071 atm)
# Trench peak temperature: Mariana trench bottom temperature is 1 to 4 °C (peak = 4 °C = 277.15 K).
# Let's calculate for a range of T around 1-4 °C (274.15 - 277.15 K) and P around 100-115 MPa:

m = 0.312 # kg

for T_C in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    T = T_C + 273.15
    for P_MPa in [100, 105, 108.6, 110, 115]:
        P = P_MPa * 1e6
        rho = CP.PropsSI('D', 'T', T, 'P', P, fluid)
        V_m3 = m / rho
        V_mL = V_m3 * 1e6
        print(f'T={T_C} C, P={P_MPa} MPa: rho={rho:.2f} kg/m3, V={V_mL:.2f} mL, rounded={round(V_mL)}')
"

python3 -c "
import CoolProp.CoolProp as CP

# Standard Mariana trench pressure values commonly cited:
# 1) 1086 bar = 108.6 MPa
# 2) 1100 bar = 110 MPa
# 3) 1071 atm = 108.52 MPa
# 4) 112 MPa
# 5) 1000 atm = 101.325 MPa (1000 times atmospheric pressure is sometimes colloquially cited: ~1000 atm ~ 101.3 MPa, giving 194.6 mL -> 195)
# 6) 1.1 x 10^8 Pa = 110 MPa

m = 0.312
T = 277.15 # 4 deg C (peak temperature of Mariana Trench bottom is 1 to 4 °C)

for P_bar in [1000, 1050, 1071, 1086, 1100, 1120, 1150]:
    P = P_bar * 1e5
    rho = CP.PropsSI('D', 'T', T, 'P', P, 'R12')
    v = m / rho * 1e6
    print(f'{P_bar} bar: rho={rho:.3f}, V={v:.4f} mL, round={round(v)}')
"
